standard_prerequisites.name: Higher inductive pushouts and their recursion principle
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a span C -f-> A, C -g-> B the pushout A sqcup^C B is generated by inl : A -> A sqcup^C B, inr : B -> A sqcup^C B and glue : Prd{c:C} inl(f(c)) = inr(g(c)); its recursion principle defines a map s : A sqcup^C B -> D from values on the three generators, with the computation rule mapfunc{s}(glue(c)) = the given path.
standard_prerequisites.use: The inverse direction of the equivalence is defined exactly by this recursion principle at source lines 971-976, and the second round trip uses the computation rule for glue at source lines 1003-1005.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cocones under a span
standard_prerequisites.statement: A cocone under D = (A <-f- C -g-> B) with vertex D is a triple (i,j,h) with i : A -> D, j : B -> D and h : Prd{c:C} i(f(c)) = j(g(c)); the type of such cocones is written cocone(D,D).
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement is an equivalence between A sqcup^C B -> E and cocone(D,E), and the retained context supplies the author's own definition of the latter.

standard_prerequisites.name: Function extensionality and paths between sigma-type elements
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two functions are equal as soon as they are homotopic; equality of triples in a sigma type is componentwise.
standard_prerequisites.use: The second round trip at source lines 996-1006 concludes equality of maps A sqcup^C B -> E after comparing values on inl, inr and glue.

core_obligations: Define the canonical map c_sqcup sending t : A sqcup^C B -> E to the cocone (t o inl, t o inr, mapfunc{t} o glue) and state that the goal is that it is an equivalence (source lines 960-964).

Define the candidate inverse s(c) for c = (i,j,h) : cocone(D,E) by the recursion principle of the pushout, with s(c)(inl(a)) := i(a), s(c)(inr(b)) := j(b) and mapfunc{s(c)}(glue(x)) := h(x) (source lines 966-976).

Check the first round trip c -> s(c) -> c inside the cocone type: unfold the composite, rewrite the three components by the defining clauses, and conclude by the definitional equality (i,j,h) (source lines 981-994).

Check the second round trip t -> c_sqcup(t) -> t as an equality of functions, by comparing the two maps on inl(a), on inr(b) and on glue(x), where the glue case is exactly the recursion computation rule (source lines 996-1006).

proof_roadmap.step: Write down the canonical map from maps out of the pushout to cocones and reduce the statement to its being an equivalence.
Build the inverse by pushout recursion on the three generators.
First round trip in the cocone type, by unfolding and the defining clauses.
Second round trip as an equality of functions, constructor by constructor.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 6.8.2 at source lines 953-957: for every type E the canonical map sending t : A sqcup^C B -> E to the cocone (t o inl, t o inr, mapfunc{t} o glue) is an equivalence with cocone(D,E). The author's 52-line proof (source lines 958-1009) is a concrete quasi-inverse construction rather than a citation: the inverse s(c) is defined by the pushout's recursion principle on the three generators inl, inr and glue (lines 971-976), and the two round trips live in different types, one in cocone(D,E) and one in a function type into E, so each has to be checked separately. The first round trip (lines 981-994) is a four-step computation that ends only at the definitional equality (i,j,h); the second (lines 996-1006) requires comparing two functions on all three constructors, and the glue case is precisely where the recursion computation rule mapfunc{s(c)}(glue(x)) = h(x) is consumed. Nothing in the statement records that the two directions are the two different comparisons.
